title: Transient connection shepherd and ephemeral-state scrubber hotpatch
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: We saw a recurring incident pattern where transient network flaps during regional failover caused a storm of reconnects that amplified KV cache divergence and tripped local circuit breakers, resulting in degraded SLOs for a subset of customers. This hotpatch introduces a two-part defensive mitigation: (1) a transient connection shepherd that applies a short, adaptive admission throttle and staggered reconnect guidance to clients that rapidly re-enter after disconnects; (2) an ephemeral-state scrubber that opportunistically detects and repairs stale in-memory KV cache markers after a node rejoin/restore window. Together these reduce oscillation during regional failovers and provide a graceful degradation path that preserves P99 latency SLOs. Design summary: - Transient connection shepherd: per-connection lightweight state machine that records disconnect timestamps and recent reconnect rate; on flood it returns a well-formed 429 with Retry-After and a small jittered backoff header usable by SDKs. Throttle thresholds are conservative and region-configurable (defaults derived from observed normal reconnect quantiles). The shepherd is implemented as a minimal pre-auth admission filter in the ingress path to avoid touching hot execution paths. - Ephemeral-state scrubber: background task that runs during node restore windows and cross-checks KV cache tombstone versions against the durable-backed sequence. If a monotonic gap is detected the scrubber re-fetches the missing keys from the durable store and rehydrates the in-memory cache or marks the connection as needing a kv-snapshot resync. The scrubber is bounded (rate-limited) and runs only when the node is under low CPU pressure to avoid adding load during failover. Safety and SLO ties: the shepherd ties into the SLO-enforcer by emitting a metric with the throttle budget consumption and a signal that we can evaluate in the console. The scrubber emits kv-coherence-mismatch and repair-duration metrics so we can alert on repair churn vs success. Backwards compatibility: the 429+Retry-After is non-breaking; SDKs will gracefully backoff. The scrubber only repairs in-memory state and does not alter durable store content. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for shepherd threshold calculus, backoff jitter, and header emission. - Integration test harness simulating regional disconnect bursts and verifying that P95/P99 latencies for existing stable clients stay within 10% of baseline. - Canary rollout in us-west-2 for 2 hours, then eu-west-1 for 4 hours with automated rollback if P99 latency increases by >15% or kv-coherence-mismatch >1% of requests. Observability and telemetry: new metrics (transient_reconnect_rate, shepherd_throttle_count, kv_coherence_mismatch, kv_repair_count, kv_repair_latency) and traces instrumented for repair flows. Added console dashboard and a Temporal alert: kv_repair_failure_rate > 0.5% over 5m. Rollout plan: - Deploy to canary fleet (us-west-2) as soft enable (no throttle; scrubber dry-run) - After 2h examine metrics; enable shepherd throttle at 10% of full sensitivity - 4h later, if stable, promote scrubber to active repair and gradually increase shepherd sensitivity to default. - Full rollout across regions over 48h with metric gating. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: scrubber could amplify load if many keys require healing. Mitigation: rate-limit repairs and use CPU/backpressure gates; scrubber will abort and escalate via alert if repair backlog climbs. - Risk: SDKs not honoring Retry-After header. Mitigation: conservative default throttle and prepend a short client-facing advisory in the API status page; plan SDK updates in parallel. Related work and context: ties to ENG-5721 (regional failover hardening) and SUP-1324 (customer reports during incident INC-2026-02-12). Not a permanent replacement for more comprehensive KV replication fixes; this is an emergency stability shim. Checklist: [x] Unit tests added [x] Integration harness updated [x] New metrics + dashboards [x] Canary rollout plan documented [x] Security review completed (ingress filter minimal privileges) Monitoring during canary: watch P50/P95/P99 latency, shepherd_throttle_count, kv_coherence_mismatch, kv_repair_latency. Post-merge: run the full canary and file a follow-up ticket to replace the scrubber with a safe streaming sync once we finish the replication design (ENG-5803).
